main_text.head: CAPUT XIV. DE JUSTINO THRACE ET TIBERIO II.
main_text.p: Iustinianum JUSTINUS Curopalates, [illegible, ~3 letters] praefectus, ejusdem ex lororem nepos [?] cujus Cariorum [?] cum jux Sophia Theodorae Augustae [?] ipsis excepit. Res ab ipso gestae [?] tum [?] ... [illegible, ~6 letters] poffunt. In prima, quae ab initio usque Curopalates ad deditum in Collatam Tiberium [?] exvendit, Justinus Justin. [?] Constitutum, populo flagitante, in Remub[?] reduxit, eidemque donativum mor[?] distribuit. Turcarum, gratis tum ad [?] Tiberius Eurum versus, legatis, ne Avares hostes [?] Justin [?]imos in amicitiam reciperet, petentibus, [?] Avarum nuncios, pactum à Iustinia- no ... [illegible, ~5 letters] exigentes, inanes remissi. Lasà Iustiniano adversus illicita coniugia leges abro- Cap. 1. gavit, & d[?] rimi matrimonia possent ex conjugum [?] volui. Armenios & Iberos, a Persis [?] dolorosa abhorrentes, in fidem recepit. Nardi[?] a Romanis accusatum, quod te[?] rios Iob Dominum quam Gothi, foret, exauthorauit. Infidus [?] titus Justinum cognatum, suprema [?] illius Magistratum, suspectum, interfecit, ei- Syncell. cap. 1. demque Arthetium & Addaeum Senatores adjecit. Bulgaros Thraciam infestantes per Tiberium trans Istrum removit. In Africa cum Mauris & in Asia cum Persis, invitato prius in societatem Aethiopum Rege Areta, bella gessit.

page.notes: Much of the page is badly faded and stained, especially the left and right margins and the middle lines. Many words are doubtful and marked [?]; longer damaged stretches are not reliably readable and are only partly transcribed. Marginal note placement and wording on the right are approximate. The running head and the year figure at the head of the chapter are doubtful. The Greek-derived name forms and the margin references could not be confirmed.
